They expect us to swallow the official narrative of random coincidence and sudden heroism coming straight out of JFK International Airport on Thursday. We are told to believe that an Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent just happened to "jump into action" when a baby stuck in a crowded TSA line supposedly stopped breathing, and the Department of Homeland Security happily releases "video footage" of it. It is all a managed spectacle designed to manufacture consent and polish the public image of border enforcement apparatuses. The timing, the cameras rolling, the precise orchestration—it is a textbook distraction maneuver orchestrated by the hidden elites pulling the strings behind the DHS to make you love the very agencies tightening the grip of surveillance and control. Do not fall for it.
